passages.text: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives is the lower house of the bicameral Pennsylvania General Assembly, the legislature of the U.S. state of Pennsylvania. There are 203 members, elected for two-year terms from single member districts.[2][3]

The following is an alphabetical list of members of the United States House of Representatives from the commonwealth of Pennsylvania. For chronological tables of members of both houses of the United States Congress from the state (through the present day), see United States Congressional Delegations from Pennsylvania. The list of names should be complete (as of October 21, 2017), but other data may be incomplete.

Republican candidates include U.S. Representative Lou Barletta,[119] Pennsylvania House of Representatives members Rick Saccone[126] and Jim Christiana,[122] Berwick councilman Andrew Shecktor,[127] Paul Addis,[117] Cynthia Ayers,[118] Jeff Bartos,[120] Paul DeLong,[123] and Robert "Bobby" Lawrence.[125]

The Delaware House of Representatives is the lower house of the Delaware General Assembly; the state legislature of the US state of Delaware. It is composed of 41 Representatives from an equal number of constituencies, each of whom is elected to a two-year term. Its members are not subject to term limits. The House meets at the Delaware Legislative Hall in Dover.

The 2018 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania will take place on November 6, 2018, to elect a member of the United States Senate to represent the State of Pennsylvania, concurrently with other elections to the United States Senate, elections to the United States House of Representatives, and various state and local elections. The primary elections will be held on May 15.[1]

reference.answer: There are 203 members in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives.
